# The calls to RANDOM under lisp/nova-work/tests/ that are not naming a path,
# one `file:definition` per line with its reason.
#
# Why the rule exists (nova-tools#1699): SBCL saves `*random-state*` into its
# core, so a FRESH IMAGE RETURNS THE SAME SEQUENCE. Measured 2026-09-19, three
# separate images, three calls each to `(random 1000000)`:
#
#     run: 113500 958198 129774
#     run: 113500 958198 129774
#     run: 113500 958198 129774
#
# The AF_UNIX fixtures in slice-05 and slice-12 named their socket directories
# from that number, so two concurrent suites agreed on the path exactly -- and
# `short-socket-base` then deleted that directory tree before binding, taking the
# other suite's live socket with it. A name from RANDOM in a fresh SBCL image is
# a constant, not a nonce, and nothing in the code says so. Path names now come
# from `test-short-tag`.
#
# `run-all` reseeds `*random-state*` from this run's entropy before the first
# case, so a call listed here really is random -- but it is listed anyway,
# because the reseed is one line somebody could delete and this list is where a
# reader finds out that it matters.
#
# lisp/nova-work/tests/harness.lisp is not listed and is not scanned: it draws
# the entropy and does the reseeding. See lispHelperHome in
# lisptemppath_class_test.go.
#
# Checked in BOTH directions, so it can only ever shrink.

lisp/nova-work/tests/replays-8642.lisp:async-operations  # names a staged-input id, never a filesystem path: the case needs more ids than the staged-input limit and does not care which
